walkthrough: Start from the given datum: $E_p = 0$ at the starting position, so initial mechanical energy $= E_{k,initial} + 0 = E_{k,initial}$.
Use the energy rule for rising: gravity does negative work so $E_k$ is transferred to $E_p$, but air resistance also does negative work so total $E_k + E_p$ slowly decreases.

At the top of the path the ball momentarily stops before falling, so $v = 0$ and $E_k = 0$. The $E_p = mgh_{max}$ there is the remaining mechanical energy, less than $E_{k,initial}$ because of heating of air.
At the midpoint of the path $h = h_{max}/2$, so $E_p = mgh_{max}/2$, about half the top value. The ball is still moving upward there, so $E_k > 0$.
Hence $E_p$ at the midpoint cannot equal the whole initial $E_k$; it is much smaller since energy is shared between $E_k$ and $E_p$ and some is already lost. This is option B.
